Despite this potent poison, Hisuian Sneasel is specifically described as lacking much of the spitefulness associated with the Johtonian form, a behavioral difference believed to result from their contrasting environments. Its combination of cliff-dwelling locomotion, poison, and a less malicious temperament eventually leads it toward Sneasler rather than Weavile.

pokemon.name: Sneasler
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sneasler is a solitary apex predator of Hisui's frozen highlands, combining extraordinary climbing ability with long poisonous claws and far greater physical strength than its lanky build suggests. Its venom and direct power are described as so formidable that no other Pokemon in its natural habitat could defeat it, allowing Sneasler to dominate the cliffside ecosystem without relying on the coordinated packs used by Weavile. The claws let it scale sheer walls and mountains with ease while also serving as the source of its signature Dire Claw attack. Although ordinary Sneasler prefer solitude, a special individual revered in Hisui descended from one of the ancient Pokemon blessed by Arceus and willingly assisted humans as a Ride Pokemon.

playthrough: The Teddiursa line develops from a modest Normal-type into one of the strongest slow physical attackers available in modern games. Teddiursa evolves into Ursaring at level 30, gaining base 130 Attack and useful HP, while Guts or Quick Feet can reward status and strong Normal STAB such as Facade can turn Ursaring into an effective wallbreaker despite base 55 Speed. In Pokemon Legends: Arceus, Ursaring can evolve into Ursaluna when exposed to a Peat Block during a full moon, gaining Ground/Normal typing, base 140 Attack, 130 HP, 105 Defense, an Electric immunity, and powerful Ground STAB at the cost of becoming slightly slower. Ursaluna is exceptionally strong when it can use Guts alongside moves such as Facade and Headlong Rush or Earthquake, but weaknesses to Water, Grass, Ice, and Fighting and low Speed mean it often has to absorb damage before attacking. Bloodmoon Ursaluna is a separate unique individual rather than a normal evolution; where obtainable, it reverses the species' usual offensive profile with base 135 Special Attack, the Mind's Eye ability, and its signature special attack Blood Moon.
competitive: Ursaring was already a dangerous lower-tier wallbreaker before Ursaluna existed, using base 130 Attack and abilities such as Guts or Quick Feet to turn status into offensive momentum, but middling bulk and base 55 Speed limited its consistency against faster teams. Regular Ursaluna raises that concept to an extreme: base 140 Attack, huge physical bulk, Ground/Normal STAB, Flame Orb, Guts, Facade, and Headlong Rush combine to create a wallbreaker capable of overpowering even many dedicated physical walls. Its low Speed remains the main check on that power, encouraging bulky offense, Trick Room support, or strategies that accept trading Ursaluna for multiple opposing Pokemon. Bloodmoon Ursaluna is instead a special attacker with base 135 Special Attack, high physical Defense, Mind's Eye, and the extremely strong Blood Moon; this form proved powerful enough to be placed in Ubers in Smogon's Generation IX singles environment. The family therefore contains two elite modern wallbreakers that share Ground/Normal typing and low Speed but attack from opposite sides of the physical/special divide.
nuzlocke: Teddiursa and Ursaring can be very strong Nuzlocke Pokemon because pure Normal typing is simple to plan around, providing a Ghost immunity and only a Fighting weakness while high Attack allows them to finish many neutral matchups quickly. Ursaring's mediocre Speed means it frequently takes a hit before attacking, so its offensive strength should not be confused with defensive safety, particularly against strong special attacks. If regular Ursaluna is obtainable, the enormous HP and physical Defense create a much larger margin for error while Ground typing adds an Electric immunity and valuable STAB, although Water, Grass, Ice, and Fighting attacks become clear dangers. Guts can make burns or poison offensively beneficial, but residual damage still matters in permadeath play and deliberately activating Guts should be weighed against the health lost between battles. Bloodmoon Ursaluna is normally a unique special encounter rather than an evolution from the player's Ursaring, but if a ruleset allows it, its bulk and enormous special offense make it exceptionally powerful despite the same low-Speed risk.

pokemon.name: Teddiursa
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Teddiursa is intensely fond of honey and habitually licks its paws because they remain soaked with the sweet substance, giving each individual's palms a distinctive flavor. It can produce its own honey-like mixture from fruit and pollen gathered by Beedrill, but it also follows Combee to their hives and steals the honey they have accumulated. Before winter food becomes scarce, Teddiursa hides supplies in multiple secret locations, showing a strong seasonal hoarding instinct despite its small size. Its crescent marking is said to glow when it discovers honey, and nervous individuals lick their sweet paws as a self-soothing behavior that quickly improves their mood.

pokemon.name: Ursaring
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Ursaring inhabits mountainous forests, sleeping in treetops despite its heavy build and spending much of the day gathering fruit, Berries, and especially honey. Instead of delicately climbing for every piece of food, it may simply snap or shake trees and collect what falls, marking particularly productive trees within its territory with scratches from its claws. Its sense of smell is exceptionally sensitive and can locate food buried underground or hidden in streams, allowing Ursaring to continue foraging even during winter. Adults are fiercely protective of their cubs and can become more aggressive when hungry or during mating season, and conflicts with other foragers such as Primeape have been documented around valuable food sources. In the swampy environment of ancient Hisui, exposure to peat during a full moon can trigger evolution into Ursaluna.

pokemon.name: Ursaluna
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Ursaluna is believed to have arisen when Ursaring adapted to Hisui's swampy terrain, developing a massive, resilient body capable of moving through deep mud and manipulating peat. Its sense of smell is extraordinary even by the standards of Ursaring, allowing it to locate buried objects and track missing people across the landscape. A revered Ursaluna in Hisui descended from one of the ancient Pokemon blessed by Arceus and used these tracking abilities to assist humans as a Ride Pokemon. The species appears to have become very uncommon in the modern era, suggesting that the environmental conditions that once supported its evolution are no longer widespread.

pokemon.name: Ursaluna
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Bloodmoon Ursaluna is not an ordinary evolutionary form but a unique, extremely old individual known as the 'Bloodmoon Beast' that once lived in Hisui before crossing the sea and eventually reaching Kitakami. Surviving for years in the Timeless Woods altered its body and abilities: iron-hard mud covers much of its body, while its unusual left eye can see clearly in darkness. It is highly alert, rarely allows itself to be seen, and is especially associated with foggy nights, which helped it survive despite becoming an object of local legend and scientific interest. The red blood-moon marking on its forehead can release tremendous spiritual power and is also treated as a vulnerable point, while the unique ability Mind's Eye and the move Blood Moon reflect powers not seen in ordinary Ursaluna. Unlike standard Ursaluna, Bloodmoon Ursaluna is not known to evolve from Ursaring or into any other Pokemon.

playthrough: The Slugma line is a very slow special Fire family whose final evolution trades the simple defensive profile of pure Fire for the much more polarized Fire/Rock typing. Slugma evolves into Magcargo at level 38, a relatively late evolution for a Pokemon with weak unevolved stats, but Magcargo gains base 120 Defense, useful Special Attack, and access to Fire and Rock STAB alongside support such as Recover, Yawn, Will-O-Wisp, screens, or Stealth Rock depending on generation. Fire/Rock supplies several useful resistances and makes Magcargo particularly comfortable against many physical Fire-, Normal-, Flying-, Bug-, Ice-, or Poison-type attacks, but it also creates quadruple weaknesses to both Water and Ground and additional weaknesses to Fighting and Rock. Beginning in Generation VII, Magcargo received modest stat increases to HP and Special Attack, improving its ability to function as a bulky special attacker without fixing the fundamental Speed and typing problems. Flame Body can punish contact with burns and Magma Armor prevents freezing, but base 30 Speed means Magcargo usually has to survive an attack before contributing.
competitive: Magcargo has generally remained in low competitive tiers because its excellent base 120 Defense and reliable recovery are undermined by very common quadruple Water and Ground weaknesses, low HP, and terrible Speed. When the matchup is favorable, however, it can function as a specialized physical wall using Recover, Lava Plume or Will-O-Wisp, Stealth Rock, Toxic, Yawn, and Flame Body to punish contact attackers and accumulate residual damage. Its Fire/Rock typing can let it answer certain Normal-, Flying-, Fire-, Bug-, and Ice-type attackers that struggle to hit it effectively, giving Magcargo narrow but legitimate defensive niches in some lower-tier metagames. Weak Armor offers a more offensive alternative and Magma Armor blocks freezing, but neither ability is normally as broadly useful as Flame Body on defensive sets. Slugma itself has occasionally experimented with Little Cup support sets using screens, Memento, recovery, and burns, but poor bulk and base 20 Speed leave it heavily outclassed by stronger Fire-types.
nuzlocke: The Slugma line is difficult to use safely in a Nuzlocke because Slugma is extremely slow and fragile before its level-38 evolution, creating a long period in which training it can require substantial protection. Magcargo becomes genuinely sturdy against physical neutral attacks and Flame Body can punish contact moves, but the quadruple Water and Ground weaknesses are severe enough that even moderate coverage can cause an immediate knockout. Its low Speed compounds that danger because it usually cannot remove a threatening opponent before taking the first hit, while its good Defense does much less against strong special Water attacks. Recover, burns, Yawn, and status support can make known favorable matchups quite safe, and Fire/Rock typing provides useful resistances when the opposing moveset is predictable. The line therefore rewards detailed opponent knowledge but is a poor blind switch-in, especially in regions where Water and Ground coverage are common.

pokemon.name: Slugma
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Slugma is a living mass of molten material whose circulatory system consists of magma carrying nutrients and oxygen through the body. It never truly sleeps and must keep moving because allowing its internal magma to cool would harden the body, make it brittle, and eventually cause pieces to break away. Slugma therefore spends its life searching for heat, gathering with others of its species around volcanoes and unusually warm mountain areas and bathing in magma to restore itself. When volcanic activity was more widespread in the distant past, Slugma is believed to have been correspondingly more common. Its entire daily behavior is governed by a basic biological necessity that ordinary animals do not share: continuous movement and external heat are required simply to prevent the body from solidifying.

pokemon.name: Magcargo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Magcargo remains composed largely of molten magma, with an internal temperature described as exceeding 18,000 degrees Fahrenheit, or about 10,000 degrees Celsius—hot enough for water touching its body to evaporate immediately. Its apparent shell is actually hardened magma; despite looking massive and protective, it is surprisingly brittle and can crack easily, allowing flames circulating inside the body to escape through the fractures. Damage to the shell is not necessarily permanent because Magcargo can immerse itself in magma and reform the hardened structure. The species has occupied volcanic craters for tens of thousands of years, and folklore claims that a sudden increase in wild Magcargo can warn of an approaching volcanic eruption. Its biology therefore combines an almost impossibly hot internal body with a shell whose fragility forces Magcargo to rely on the very volcanic environments that created it for repair.

playthrough: The Swinub line develops into a powerful Ice/Ground physical attacker, but its effectiveness changes dramatically across generations. Swinub evolves into Piloswine at level 33, and in Generations II and III Piloswine is the final stage; Ground attacks such as Earthquake already use its strong Attack in those games, but Ice attacks are special before Generation IV and therefore do not take advantage of its better physical offense. From Generation IV onward, a Piloswine that levels up while knowing Ancient Power evolves into Mamoswine, gaining base 130 Attack, 110 HP, and enough Speed to function as an imposing wallbreaker rather than merely a slow bulky attacker. Physical Ice options such as Ice Shard, Ice Fang, Icicle Crash, and later Icicle Spear pair naturally with Ground STAB, giving Mamoswine excellent coverage against Dragon-, Flying-, Grass-, Electric-, Ground-, Rock-, and Steel-related matchups depending on the move being used. Its main drawback is a broad weakness profile—Fire, Water, Grass, Fighting, and Steel all hit it super effectively—so Mamoswine is strongest when its excellent offensive coverage and Electric immunity are used proactively rather than as an excuse to absorb unknown attacks.
competitive: Mamoswine immediately established a serious competitive niche when it debuted in Generation IV, reaching OU through the combination of base 130 Attack and an Ice/Ground STAB pairing that very few Pokemon could switch into safely. Earthquake provides extremely reliable Ground damage while physical Ice STAB threatens Dragons, Ground-types, Flying-types, and Grass-types, and Ice Shard gives Mamoswine valuable priority that compensates for its only moderate base 80 Speed. Later generations added Thick Fat as a Hidden Ability, effectively reducing damage from Fire and Ice attacks and giving Mamoswine more opportunities to enter battle despite its otherwise awkward defensive typing. Choice Band, Life Orb, Stealth Rock, Focus Sash lead, and mixed utility sets have all appeared across generations because Mamoswine combines immediate power with useful priority and an Electric immunity. Its weaknesses to common Water-, Grass-, Fighting-, Steel-, and Fire-type attacks, plus mediocre Special Defense, prevent it from functioning as a conventional tank, but its offensive typing has kept it relevant well beyond the generation in which it was introduced.
nuzlocke: The Swinub line can become an excellent Nuzlocke attacker, especially from Generation IV onward when Mamoswine exists and physical Ice attacks align with its enormous Attack. Its high HP and respectable physical bulk provide more room for error than many Ice-type attackers, while the Electric immunity creates predictable safe switches and Ice Shard can finish weakened enemies without allowing them another turn. The danger is that Ice/Ground is weak to all three traditional starter types—Fire, Water, and Grass—as well as Fighting and Steel, so Mamoswine can encounter super-effective coverage in many otherwise unrelated battles. Swinub and Piloswine also require patience before reaching their strongest form, with Piloswine evolving at level 33 and Mamoswine requiring access to Ancient Power in games where that evolution exists. Used against known Electric-, Dragon-, Flying-, Ground-, or other favorable targets, Mamoswine can be one of the strongest Nuzlocke finishers available, but its large weakness list makes blind switching unnecessarily risky.

pokemon.name: Swinub
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Swinub is a small cold-climate Pokemon covered in dense shaggy fur that insulates its body in icy caves, mountains, and frozen tundra. Its strongest sense is smell: it continually roots through mud, snow, and dead grass with its sensitive nose in search of anything edible, especially a particular type of mushroom that grows beneath dead vegetation. When Swinub detects an appealing scent it may abandon caution and run desperately toward the source, and this same digging ability has allowed both wild Pokemon and humans to discover buried food, objects, and even hot springs. Ancient people in Hisui relied heavily on Swinub's ability to locate things hidden below the ground, making its natural foraging behavior useful to human communities as well as to the Pokemon itself.

pokemon.name: Piloswine
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Piloswine's body is covered in such long, thick fur that its eyes and short legs are usually almost completely hidden, allowing it to withstand exceptionally cold environments. Because its vision is obstructed, it relies heavily on its sensitive nose and ears to understand its surroundings and may simply charge repeatedly toward a detected threat. Its rugged hooves provide reliable traction on ice despite its short legs, while its tusks are made of ice and become thicker when snow falls. Piloswine uses those tusks not only as weapons but also to dig through packed snow and frozen ground in search of buried food.

pokemon.name: Mamoswine
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mamoswine is an Ice Age survivor covered in exceptionally thick fur and armed with enormous tusks made of solid ice, which grow longer and more impressive as temperatures fall. The species once flourished across much of the world during the last ice age but became far less common as the climate warmed and permanent ice receded. Its tolerance of cold and starvation is extraordinary: a Mamoswine frozen for roughly ten thousand years was reportedly revived after being excavated, demonstrating a level of suspended survival far beyond that of most living creatures. Mamoswine remains associated with frozen mountains and tundra, where its strength allows it to force paths through deep snow; humans in Kalos even use trained individuals as mounts to cross otherwise impassable winter terrain. Despite its size and power, Mamoswine is not beyond predation, with Weavile documented as one of its natural predators.

playthrough: The Corsola family contains two fundamentally different branches: Johtonian Corsola is a defensive Water/Rock Pokemon that does not evolve, while Galarian Corsola is a pure Ghost-type that evolves into Cursola at level 38. Johtonian Corsola is slow and only modestly offensive, but good mixed defenses, Recover, useful resistances, and abilities such as Natural Cure or Regenerator in later generations can make it a durable support Pokemon when its weaknesses are carefully avoided. Its Water/Rock typing is especially vulnerable to Grass, which hits for quadruple damage, and it is also weak to Electric, Fighting, and Ground, making matchup knowledge important despite its defensive stats. Galarian Corsola plays almost the opposite way: base 100 Defense and Special Defense, Ghost immunities to Normal and Fighting, Will-O-Wisp, Strength Sap, and Eviolite can make the unevolved form exceptionally difficult to break, while evolving into Cursola trades much of that physical security for base 145 Special Attack and 130 Special Defense. Cursola is therefore a powerful but extremely slow special attacker, whereas Galarian Corsola itself can be the safer choice for players who value defensive reliability over damage.
competitive: Johtonian Corsola has generally remained in low competitive tiers, but it possesses a real defensive toolkit through Recover, Stealth Rock, Scald or other Water STAB, status, Natural Cure, and especially Regenerator. Its respectable mixed defenses allow it to check selected attackers, yet Water/Rock typing creates several common weaknesses—including a quadruple Grass weakness—and low Speed and offensive pressure make it easier to exploit than stronger defensive Pokemon. Galarian Corsola briefly became much more notable because Eviolite multiplies its already excellent base 100 defenses, while Strength Sap, Will-O-Wisp, Night Shade, Stealth Rock, and Cursed Body allow it to function as an exceptionally stubborn physical wall. Cursola instead possesses an enormous base 145 Special Attack and 130 Special Defense, but base 50 Defense and base 30 Speed make it vulnerable to physical attackers before it can exploit that power; Perish Body can punish contact but is not enough to solve the underlying fragility. The family therefore has an unusual competitive situation in which the unevolved Galarian form can occupy a more useful defensive niche than its evolution, while Cursola is primarily a slow special wallbreaker.
nuzlocke: Johtonian Corsola can be useful in a Nuzlocke because Recover and solid defenses give it genuine staying power, and Natural Cure or Regenerator can improve its ability to recover from status or repeated switching in games where those abilities are available. Its quadruple Grass weakness is a severe hazard, however, and Electric, Ground, and Fighting coverage also make it unsafe to use as a blind defensive switch simply because its defenses are high. Galarian Corsola can be one of the safer defensive Pokemon in its game when holding Eviolite, with Normal and Fighting immunities, excellent effective bulk, Strength Sap, burns, and recovery-based play offering a large margin for error against known physical opponents. Evolving into Cursola is not automatically an upgrade for a permadeath run: Cursola gains extraordinary Special Attack and special bulk but drops to base 50 Defense and loses the Eviolite boost, making physical mistakes much more dangerous. For a Nuzlocke, keeping Galarian Corsola unevolved can therefore be a legitimate long-term strategy rather than merely delaying evolution.

pokemon.name: Corsola
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Johtonian Corsola lives in clean, warm, shallow seas and forms large colonies whose branching coral-like growths can collectively become substantial enough for people to build communities above them. Its branches glitter in multiple colors under sunlight and continually shed and regrow; a broken branch can be replaced in as little as a single night. The species is extremely sensitive to water quality, with polluted habitats causing its colorful growths to discolor and degenerate, making healthy Corsola a visible indicator of clean marine conditions. Small Pokemon such as Horsea and Luvdisc may shelter among its branches, while in Alola Mareanie and Toxapex prey directly on those branches and can force Corsola to break them off as decoys while escaping. Humans prize shed Corsola material for jewelry, carving, and traditional charms, creating a long-standing cultural relationship with the species.

pokemon.name: Corsola
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Galarian Corsola represents the ghostly remains of an ancient Corsola population that was wiped out after sudden changes in climate and ocean temperature destroyed its marine habitat. Its bleached shell resembles dead coral, while the translucent branches surrounding it are incorporeal projections that can disappear and reform at will. Those ghostly branches cannot injure a victim through ordinary physical force, but they can take root inside another creature, immobilize it, and drain away life energy. Galarian Corsola often remain among the fossilized remnants of prehistoric seas and can be mistaken for ordinary stones; people who accidentally kick one are said to be cursed. Continuous feeding on spiritual energy eventually causes the remaining shell to break apart, allowing the ghostly body within to emerge fully as Cursola.

pokemon.name: Cursola
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cursola consists of a broken coral shell surrounded by an enormous ectoplasmic body produced after years of absorbing spiritual energy from other living beings. The ectoplasm is hazardous to touch and can leave a victim's body stiff as stone, making even accidental physical contact dangerous. Despite the eerie appearance, Cursola is so light that it moves with a characteristic wobbling motion and may appear almost buoyant compared with its former shell-bound body. Groups gather beneath the full moon and raise their spectral branches toward the sky, but researchers have not determined whether this behavior releases accumulated spirit energy, serves as communication, or performs some other ritual function. Its unique Perish Body ability mirrors the species' dangerous physical presence by causing creatures that make contact with it to become caught in a countdown toward fainting.

playthrough: The Remoraid line is unusual because its unevolved and evolved forms look almost unrelated, but both are built around ranged attacks and broad offensive coverage. Remoraid evolves into Octillery at level 25, after which both Attack and Special Attack reach base 105, allowing physical, special, or mixed sets depending on the generation and available moves. Octillery is particularly notable for special coverage far beyond that of most Water-types, with combinations such as Surf or Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Fire Blast, Energy Ball, Psychic, and other options letting it target many common Water answers. Its major limitation is base 45 Speed and merely average 75/75/75 bulk, so Octillery often has to take a hit before using that excellent coverage and can be overwhelmed by stronger or faster attackers. Suction Cups prevents forced switching, Sniper can strengthen critical hits, and Moody can produce extreme stat swings in games where it is available, but ordinary playthroughs usually benefit more from Octillery's straightforward offensive movepool than from building around unreliable random boosts.
competitive: Octillery has rarely escaped low competitive tiers despite possessing excellent mixed offenses and one of the broadest special coverage movepools among Water-types. Base 105 Attack and Special Attack let it threaten would-be counters with moves such as Hydro Pump, Fire Blast, Ice Beam, Energy Ball, and Gunk Shot, while Sniper can support critical-hit-focused sets and Suction Cups prevents opposing phazing moves from forcing it out. The problem is base 45 Speed combined with only average bulk, which means faster attackers often remove Octillery before it can exploit its coverage and bulkier Water-types can usually perform defensive or offensive roles more efficiently. Its Hidden Ability Moody has historically been banned or heavily restricted in many standard singles environments because the automatic random stat changes can create uncompetitive snowballing, so competitive Octillery is generally evaluated without relying on it. The result is a Pokemon with genuinely threatening move selection but insufficient Speed and durability to convert that versatility into consistent high-level success.
nuzlocke: Remoraid can become useful quickly in a Nuzlocke because it evolves into Octillery at level 25 and does not require a stone, trade, or friendship condition. Octillery's pure Water typing leaves only Grass and Electric weaknesses, while equal base 105 offenses and enormous coverage let it adapt its moveset to whatever gaps the rest of the team has. Its main weakness is tempo: base 45 Speed means it will often take a hit before acting, and base 75 defenses are not high enough to make repeated strong neutral attacks comfortable in a permadeath run. Because Octillery can attack from either side, it can exploit opponents with lopsided defenses more easily than many Water-types, but the player should still avoid asking it to absorb unknown Electric or Grass coverage. It is a flexible and often underrated team member when encountered, but it is safer as a deliberate coverage attacker than as a universal defensive Water-type.

pokemon.name: Remoraid
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Remoraid is an exceptionally accurate aquatic hunter capable of firing concentrated jets of water from its mouth at moving targets more than 300 feet, or roughly 100 meters, away. It generates the pressure with powerful abdominal muscles and uses the technique to knock flying prey such as Burmy out of the air, earning the species the nickname 'sniper of the seas.' The same water jets can be fired in reverse to propel Remoraid backward when it needs to escape danger. Its dorsal fin functions like a suction pad, allowing Remoraid to attach beneath Mantine, eat scraps left behind by its host, travel with it, and even help defend it against attackers. Remoraid also gather in schools of their own kind and may move downstream from rivers toward the sea as evolution approaches.

pokemon.name: Octillery
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Octillery is a marine ambush predator with eight strongly suctioned tentacles, a rock-hard head, and an instinctive attraction to holes, rocky crevices, and even human-made pots that can serve as shelters. It may seize prey with its suction cups and then strike with its hardened head, or spray the target with dark ink before tightening its grip. That ink does more than obscure vision: it contains substances that dull a predator's sense of smell, helping Octillery escape while also protecting its young, and humans can use the ink as a cooking ingredient. Wild Octillery can be stubborn enough to steal another individual's nesting hole when sleepy, while domesticated individuals are described as comparatively relaxed and fond of attention from their Trainers. Its extreme anatomical difference from Remoraid was once so confusing that people doubted the two Pokemon could genuinely belong to the same evolutionary line.

playthrough: Delibird is a single-stage Ice/Flying Pokemon whose charming concept is unfortunately paired with very poor battle statistics. Its base 75 Speed is merely moderate and every defensive stat is extremely low, while base 55 Attack and 65 Special Attack leave it struggling to deal enough damage before taking a hit in return. Ice/Flying typing does provide a Ground immunity and useful Grass and Bug resistances, but weaknesses to Fire, Electric, Steel, and especially a quadruple Rock weakness make it one of the least forgiving fully evolved Pokemon to use in a normal story. Hustle can increase physical damage but lowers physical accuracy, while Vital Spirit or Insomnia prevent sleep; later movepools also give Delibird useful moves such as Ice Shard, Drill Peck or Brave Bird, Freeze-Dry, Spikes, Rapid Spin, and coverage. Its signature move Present is more flavorful than reliable because it can deal several different amounts of damage or heal the opponent instead, so a serious playthrough set normally benefits from using conventional attacks whenever possible.
competitive: Delibird has historically been among the weakest fully evolved Pokemon in competitive singles because its low stats and Ice/Flying typing create major problems that even a surprisingly useful support movepool cannot overcome. It has attempted lead roles with Spikes and Rapid Spin, later adding tools such as Freeze-Dry and Memento, while Hustle can give physical attacks a badly needed power increase. The same Hustle boost also reduces accuracy, however, and Delibird's 45/45/45 bulk gives it very little opportunity to recover from a miss or failed prediction. A quadruple weakness to Stealth Rock is particularly damaging in hazard-heavy generations, stripping half of Delibird's maximum HP whenever it enters through a full layer unless the hazard is removed or mitigated. Smogon analyses across multiple generations therefore consistently describe it as outclassed even in very low tiers, with its competitive interest coming mainly from unusual support options rather than genuine efficiency.
nuzlocke: Delibird is a risky Nuzlocke encounter because low bulk, mediocre Speed, and several common weaknesses leave almost no margin for unexpected damage. The quadruple Rock weakness is especially dangerous, and strong Electric, Fire, or Steel attacks can also remove it quickly despite the useful Ground immunity. Hustle can help Delibird secure knockouts that its base Attack would otherwise miss, but reduced accuracy is uniquely dangerous in a permadeath format because a single missed attack may immediately cost the Pokemon its life. Present is even less suitable as a safety tool because its random effect can produce weak damage or actually restore one quarter of the opponent's maximum HP instead of hurting it. Priority Ice Shard, sleep immunity through Vital Spirit or Insomnia, and later support moves give Delibird a few situational uses, but most Nuzlocke teams should treat it as a specialist rather than a dependable front-line battler.

pokemon.name: Delibird
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Delibird is an omnivorous mountain bird whose hollow tail functions like a natural sack in which it stores food collected throughout the day. Most of that food is carried back to its chicks, but Delibird is remarkably generous and will also share supplies with other Pokemon and with humans who become lost or stranded in dangerous mountain terrain. Its idea of suitable food can be unsettling to people: because Delibird is omnivorous, the provisions it offers a starving traveler may include captured Bug-type Pokemon as well as more familiar food. The species builds nests on steep cliffs, and within a flock the individual possessing the largest tail serves as the leader. When threatened, Delibird can turn the same stored food into ammunition and throw it at an attacker, giving its characteristic gift-carrying behavior both nurturing and defensive functions.

playthrough: The Mantyke line develops into Mantine, a Water/Flying Pokemon built primarily around enormous Special Defense rather than conventional offensive power. Mantyke evolves when it levels up while a Remoraid is present in the party, an unusual requirement that can make evolution dependent on catching a second specific Pokemon; games released before Generation IV simply provide Mantine directly because Mantyke did not yet exist. Mantine's base 140 Special Defense is exceptional, and beginning in Generation VII its base HP was increased to 85, giving it substantially better overall special bulk than in earlier generations. Water/Flying typing supplies a Ground immunity and useful resistances to Fire, Water, Fighting, Bug, and Steel, while Water Absorb can add a complete Water immunity; Surf or Scald, Air Slash, Ice Beam, Roost, Haze, and Defog or other support moves can give it both offensive and defensive utility depending on the game. The major dangers are low physical Defense, a Rock weakness, and especially a quadruple Electric weakness, making Mantine excellent against selected special attackers but extremely unsafe around unknown Electric coverage.
competitive: Mantine's competitive identity is that of a specialized special wall and utility Pokemon whose base 140 Special Defense lets it absorb attacks that would overwhelm many other Water-types. Water Absorb can turn opposing Water attacks into free healing, while Scald, Roost, Toxic, Haze, and especially Defog in relevant generations let Mantine combine defensive checking with hazard removal and anti-setup utility. Its Generation VII HP increase from 65 to 85 made this role substantially stronger, and Smogon analyses from that era highlight its ability to repeatedly switch into powerful special attackers and use those turns to clear hazards or spread status. The limitations are severe but easy to identify: a quadruple Electric weakness, susceptibility to Stealth Rock, mediocre physical Defense, and relatively passive damage output mean opponents can exploit it with the right coverage or physical wallbreakers. Mantine therefore succeeds as a role-specific special sponge rather than as a universal defensive Water-type.
nuzlocke: Mantine can be an excellent Nuzlocke specialist because enormous Special Defense and numerous useful resistances make selected special attackers extraordinarily safe to fight. Water Absorb is especially valuable when available, turning predictable Water attacks into healing opportunities, while the Ground immunity adds another source of completely safe switches. The line's danger is concentrated in a few very important places: Electric attacks deal quadruple damage, Rock attacks are super effective, and Mantine's physical Defense is much lower than its special bulk, so strong neutral physical hits can be more dangerous than its overall durability initially suggests. Mantyke itself already has excellent Special Defense but poor offenses and physical durability, and the requirement to keep a Remoraid in the party while leveling can delay evolution if that species has not yet been caught. Once evolved, Mantine is one of the safer answers to known special Water-, Fire-, Ice-, and other favorable attackers, provided the player treats Electric coverage as potentially lethal.

pokemon.name: Mantyke
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mantyke is a friendly young ray Pokemon whose two antennae are sensitive enough to detect subtle changes in ocean currents while it swims near the surface. It commonly approaches boats without fear and travels alongside schools of Remoraid, with the two species cooperating to repel attackers rather than behaving solely as predator and scavenger. Long-term association with Remoraid is directly tied to Mantyke's development into Mantine, making their ecological relationship unusually important to the Pokemon's life cycle. Mantyke is gentle and easy to tame, and people organize swimming and sightseeing tours specifically to watch groups skim and play across the tops of waves. Its back markings are said to vary between regions, while populations living in Galar's colder water appear to move more slowly than Mantyke from warmer seas.

pokemon.name: Mantine
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mantine is a large, docile open-ocean Pokemon that swims in schools and can build enough speed beneath the surface to leap roughly 300 feet, or 100 meters, into the air. Early observers sometimes mistook these enormous breaches for the flight of a bird Pokemon, illustrating how dramatically the species can leave its normal aquatic environment. Remoraid commonly attach beneath Mantine's fins using suction, feeding on scraps left behind by the larger Pokemon and helping defend it when attacked; Mantine appears entirely comfortable with this relationship. In Alola, humans ride Mantine between islands and surf waves on their backs, making the species an important part of recreation, transportation, and regional popular culture. Its combination of social schooling, tolerance of Remoraid, and calm interactions with humans makes Mantine one of the more conspicuously cooperative large marine Pokemon.

playthrough: Skarmory is a single-stage Steel/Flying Pokemon whose greatest playthrough strength is extraordinary physical durability rather than raw offensive power. Base 140 Defense, a Ground immunity, a Poison immunity, and a long list of resistances let it shut down many physical opponents, while its typing leaves only Fire and Electric as ordinary weaknesses. Its offensive stats are modest, but reliable Flying attacks such as Drill Peck or Brave Bird, Steel STAB, and later options such as Body Press allow it to deal respectable damage while support moves like Spikes, Stealth Rock, Whirlwind, Roost, and Defog can give it additional value depending on generation. Sturdy becomes much more useful from Generation V onward because a full-health Skarmory can survive a normally lethal single hit with at least 1 HP; before then, Sturdy only blocked one-hit knockout moves. Pokemon Legends: Z-A also gives Skarmory access to Mega Evolution, temporarily pushing the species beyond its traditional defensive role and giving it a much more aggressive form built around extremely fast flight and powerful talon attacks.
competitive: Skarmory has one of the most distinguished defensive careers of any non-legendary Pokemon. In Generation II it was the defining physical wall of GSC OU, where Steel/Flying typing, base 140 Defense, Whirlwind, Rest, and the absence of a physical weakness made it exceptionally difficult for conventional physical attackers such as Snorlax and Marowak to break. Generation III made it even more influential by giving it Spikes, turning Skarmory into both a premier physical wall and one of ADV OU's central hazard setters; later generations added Stealth Rock, Roost, Defog, Body Press, and the upgraded form of Sturdy while preserving its core defensive identity. Its recurring weaknesses are low HP, mediocre Special Defense, Fire and Electric attacks, and the possibility of becoming passive against special attackers or Pokemon that can exploit repeated support turns. Despite those limitations, Skarmory remained an OU-level defensive staple across numerous generations because very few Pokemon combine its physical bulk, typing, reliable recovery, phazing, and hazard utility so efficiently.
nuzlocke: Skarmory is an excellent Nuzlocke Pokemon when it can be obtained because its enormous Defense and exceptional Steel/Flying typing create a large number of safe switches against known physical attacks. Ground and Poison immunities are especially useful for planned switching, while numerous resistances let Skarmory absorb physical Normal-, Flying-, Bug-, Grass-, Psychic-, Dragon-, Steel-, and later Fairy-type attacks far more comfortably than most ordinary team members. The main danger is becoming overconfident in that bulk: powerful Fire and Electric attacks hit super effectively, and strong neutral special moves can deal far more damage than Skarmory's physical reputation suggests because its Special Defense is only average. From Generation V onward, Sturdy can function as valuable emergency insurance when Skarmory is at full HP, although prior chip damage, entry hazards, weather, and multi-hit attacks can remove that protection. Skarmory is therefore one of the safest physical pivots available in a Nuzlocke, but it should still be kept away from known special Fire- and Electric-type threats.

pokemon.name: Skarmory
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Skarmory is an armored avian Pokemon whose steel-covered body looks heavy but is built around hollow, lightweight structures that allow it to fly at roughly 185 miles per hour, or 300 kilometers per hour. Young Skarmory nest in thorny bramble bushes, and repeated scratching against the thorns gradually hardens their bodies into the armor-like state seen in adults; battered wings are completely renewed about once each year, restoring the razor edges of the feathers. Those shed feathers are sharp enough that people historically fashioned them into swords and knives, and modern cultures continue to use Skarmory imagery in heraldry and other designs. The metal body is surprisingly vulnerable to rust, causing Skarmory to remain in its nest during rainy weather, while in Galar it engages in violent territorial conflicts with Corviknight. Mega Skarmory pushes its aerial adaptations even further: it can exceed the speed of sound, using shock waves to throw opponents off balance before finishing them with enlarged, sharply armored talons.

playthrough: The Houndour line develops quickly into Houndoom, a fast special attacker whose Dark/Fire typing provides excellent offensive coverage and a complete immunity to Psychic attacks. Houndour evolves at level 24, and Houndoom's base 110 Special Attack and 95 Speed allow it to pressure Grass-, Psychic-, Ghost-, Ice-, and Steel-type opponents before many of them can respond. Unlike several other pre-split Pokemon, Houndoom was already well aligned with its stats in Generations II and III because both Fire and Dark attacks were special by type, allowing its main STAB moves to use Special Attack; later generations add tools such as Nasty Plot, Dark Pulse, and Flash Fire for even greater offensive pressure. Its major Johto drawback is availability rather than battle quality: in Gold, Silver, Crystal, HeartGold, and SoulSilver, Houndour is normally obtained in Kanto after much or all of the Johto main story has already been completed. Mega Houndoom substantially raises Special Attack and Speed and gains Solar Power, making it extremely dangerous in sun at the cost of steadily losing HP while the weather is active.
competitive: Houndoom established a legitimate competitive niche immediately in Generation II, where strong Special Attack, good Speed, Dark/Fire STAB, and the strongest Pursuit in GSC let it punish Psychic- and Ghost-type Pokemon that attempted to switch away. Its typing also made it an excellent offensive check to threats such as Jynx and Exeggutor, while Fire Blast, Crunch or Dark coverage, Sunny Day, and Pursuit gave it a combination of immediate power and trapping utility. Later generations shifted Houndoom toward Nasty Plot sweeping and Flash Fire-based opportunities, while Mega Houndoom raised its stats to a much more aggressive level and used Solar Power to become a devastating special attacker on sun teams. The family has always been held back by poor physical Defense, weaknesses to Water, Ground, Rock, and Fighting, and competition from faster or bulkier Fire- and Dark-types. Even so, Houndoom has maintained a recognizable competitive identity because few Pokemon combine its Speed, special power, useful immunities, and dual STAB in quite the same way.
nuzlocke: Houndoom can be an excellent offensive Nuzlocke Pokemon because strong Special Attack and good Speed often let it remove dangerous Psychic-, Ghost-, Grass-, Ice-, or Steel-type opponents before taking damage. Its Psychic immunity and multiple useful resistances create safe switching opportunities, while Flash Fire can add a complete Fire immunity in generations where Houndoom has that ability. The tradeoff is physical fragility: base 50 Defense makes strong neutral physical attacks dangerous, and Water, Ground, Rock, and Fighting coverage can be fatal if Houndoom is used without checking the opponent's moveset. Johto-based runs also have to account for very late availability, since Houndour is normally found in Kanto rather than during the main badge quest, sharply reducing how much of the run the line can influence. When obtained early enough in another game, Houndoom is best treated as a fast offensive specialist that enters on an immunity or resistance and immediately applies pressure rather than attempting to tank unknown hits.

pokemon.name: Houndour
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Houndour is an intelligent social predator that hunts in coordinated packs with an unusually sophisticated system of vocal communication. Different barks allow pack members to track one another's positions while surrounding prey, while eerie howls near dawn serve as territorial announcements that warn outsiders away. The cooperation extends beyond hunting: Houndour have been shown refusing to abandon sick pack members, and the species is notably loyal and obedient when it forms a bond with a Trainer. Even while asleep Houndour may howl, behavior interpreted as dreaming about hunting together with the rest of its pack.

pokemon.name: Houndoom
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Houndoom lives in packs governed by a hierarchy in which leadership is decided through combat, with the individual whose horns curve most sharply backward serving as leader. Its digestive system contains toxins that mix with the fire it produces, creating foul-smelling flames whose burns are described as causing pain that never completely disappears. After a successful hunt Houndoom divides captured prey evenly among the pack, while its terrifying howl is powerful enough to send other Pokemon fleeing back to their nests and was once mistaken by humans for the cry of the grim reaper. Mega Evolution causes Houndoom's entire body to generate such extreme heat that even its own claws become painfully hot and dark red, while its fiery breath becomes powerful enough to reduce opponents to ash or charcoal. This makes Mega Houndoom an unusual example of a transformation whose increased power is explicitly uncomfortable for the Pokemon using it.

playthrough: The Phanpy line becomes a powerful physical Ground Pokemon with exceptional Attack and Defense but low Speed and relatively weak special durability. Phanpy evolves into Donphan at level 25, after which base 120 Attack and 120 Defense make Earthquake an excellent primary weapon and allow Donphan to handle many physical Rock-, Poison-, Steel-, Fire-, and Electric-related matchups effectively. Rapid Spin gives the line valuable field or competitive-style utility in games where entry hazards matter, while Rock coverage, Knock Off, Ice Shard, Stealth Rock, and other moves can fill additional roles depending on generation. Pure Ground typing provides a complete Electric immunity and only three weaknesses—Water, Grass, and Ice—but Donphan's base 60 Special Defense means strong special attacks of those types are particularly dangerous. From Generation V onward, Sturdy can guarantee survival from full HP against a single ordinary hit, making Donphan even more dependable as a bulky physical attacker during difficult battles.
competitive: Donphan has maintained a long competitive niche as a physically powerful Rapid Spin user rather than as a pure wall or sweeper. In Generation II it already found an OU niche through Ground typing, base 120 Attack and Defense, and Rapid Spin, with useful matchups against physical staples such as Steelix, Rhydon, Tyranitar, and Raikou. DPP made Donphan especially prominent in UU, where it combined Rapid Spin, Stealth Rock, Earthquake, and excellent physical bulk, and it also saw OU use because it was one of the few hazard removers with real physical offensive presence. Ice Shard later gave it priority against weakened Flying-, Ground-, and Dragon-type targets, while the modern version of Sturdy adds emergency reliability. Its low Speed, poor Special Defense, lack of convenient reliable recovery, and weaknesses to Water, Grass, and Ice prevent it from becoming a universal defensive Pokemon, but its blend of spinning, physical bulk, and immediate Ground damage has remained useful across multiple generations.
nuzlocke: Donphan is a very dependable Nuzlocke Pokemon against physical opponents because base 120 Defense, strong Attack, and pure Ground typing provide both survivability and immediate offensive pressure. The Electric immunity creates predictable safe switches, and an early-enough Phanpy can reach Donphan at level 25 without requiring a trade, stone, friendship, or other complicated evolution condition. Its greatest weakness is special damage: Water, Grass, and Ice attacks are all super effective and often special, targeting Donphan's much weaker base 60 Special Defense rather than its impressive physical bulk. Ice Shard can reduce risk by finishing weakened enemies before they move, while modern Sturdy provides useful one-hit insurance if Donphan remains at full health. Used as a physical tank and Ground attacker rather than a general-purpose wall, Donphan offers one of the better margins for error among ordinary Johto families.

pokemon.name: Phanpy
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Phanpy is a small elephant-like Pokemon whose short trunk is both extremely sensitive and surprisingly strong, powerful enough for an affectionate playful bump to send a person flying. Its large ears function as fans for cooling, while the body is strong enough to carry an adult human despite Phanpy's small size. Wild Phanpy inhabit rocky terrain and dig vertical nesting pits near rivers, marking the surrounding area with their trunks to establish ownership. In the quiet morning hours they enter the river to wash, and groups sometimes soak one another before drying together along the riverbank.

pokemon.name: Donphan
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Donphan's back is covered by a band of extremely tough hide that resembles a tire when the Pokemon curls into a ball, allowing it to roll at high speed and deliver tackles powerful enough to knock down a house. Although normally calm, an enraged Donphan can enter a nearly unstoppable rolling rampage and pursue whatever provoked it. Rolling is also part of courtship: male Donphan have been observed competing through displays of toughness, while within wild herds individuals with larger tusks hold higher social rank. Its hide is described as tough enough to resist scratches from a car, yet the same armor is unusually vulnerable to rain, giving the species a striking environmental weakness despite its physical toughness. Donphan also possesses an excellent sense of smell and can use its trunk to locate valuable buried substances.

playthrough: Stantler is a flexible Normal-type with balanced mixed offenses, respectable Speed, broad coverage, and useful support options, but for most generations it lacked the raw specialization that allows stronger Pokemon to dominate a playthrough. Pure Normal typing gives it a Ghost immunity and only a Fighting weakness, while Intimidate from Generation III onward can make physical matchups considerably safer and Sap Sipper can provide a Grass immunity when the Hidden Ability is available. Pokemon Legends: Arceus introduces Wyrdeer, a Normal/Psychic evolution obtained after Stantler repeatedly uses Psyshield Bash in Agile Style, transforming the family into a bulkier mixed attacker with base 103 HP and 105 in both Attack and Special Attack. Wyrdeer's Psychic typing adds useful Psychic STAB and leaves it with only Bug and Dark weaknesses under ordinary conditions, while Intimidate, Calm Mind, coverage, and Psyshield Bash allow it to fill offensive or support roles. Its lower base 65 Speed means Wyrdeer is less suited to simply outrunning opponents than Stantler, but the added bulk and offensive power make it a much more substantial final-stage Pokemon.
competitive: Stantler historically occupied low competitive tiers as an adaptable but statistically unexceptional Normal-type, using combinations of Intimidate, Return or Double-Edge, Earthquake, Hypnosis, screens, Calm Mind, and broad coverage to surprise specific opponents. Its greatest problem was role competition: many other Normal-types were stronger, faster, bulkier, or possessed more specialized abilities, leaving Stantler without a uniquely compelling high-level niche. Wyrdeer improves the family's raw stats considerably and adds Normal/Psychic typing, Intimidate, Sap Sipper, Trick Room, Calm Mind, and mixed attacking potential, but its base 65 Speed and merely moderate defenses outside its large HP pool have generally kept it in lower modern tiers. In doubles, Intimidate and Trick Room-style support can give Wyrdeer additional utility, while Sap Sipper can create a surprise immunity to Grass attacks. The evolution therefore makes the family substantially more capable without turning it into a dominant competitive threat.
nuzlocke: Stantler can be a useful Nuzlocke encounter because Normal typing provides a Ghost immunity, only one ordinary weakness, and enough Speed and offensive flexibility to contribute without extensive setup. Intimidate is particularly valuable when available because it reduces physical damage immediately on entry and can turn otherwise risky switches into manageable ones. In Legends: Arceus, Wyrdeer provides a major increase in HP and offensive power while Normal/Psychic typing leaves only Bug and Dark weaknesses, giving the line a compact and easy-to-plan defensive profile. The main caution is that Wyrdeer becomes slower and still lacks exceptional raw defenses, so strong physical or special attacks can wear it down despite the impressive HP stat. Both stages reward planned use of Intimidate, immunities, and broad coverage rather than reckless neutral trading.

pokemon.name: Stantler
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Stantler's oddly shaped antlers distort the flow of air around them, producing a hypnotic effect that can make anyone staring into their curves feel as though they are being pulled inward until dizziness becomes severe enough to prevent standing. The black orbs embedded in the antlers give off a pleasant fragrance, and the unusual shape of the antlers made them historically valuable enough that excessive hunting nearly drove the species to extinction in some regions. Stantler live in herds in forests and mountainous grasslands, using their supernatural sensory abilities alongside ordinary cervid group behavior. Modern descendants appear unable to evolve under most present-day conditions, but ancient Hisuian Stantler exposed to harsher environments could develop into Wyrdeer.

pokemon.name: Wyrdeer
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Wyrdeer is a cold-adapted evolution of Stantler covered in thick insulating fur that was highly valued by the people of ancient Hisui for making warm clothing. The black orbs on its enlarged golden antlers generate extremely powerful psychic energy, allowing Wyrdeer to create invisible barriers and even distort space. It uses those antlers not only in battle but to guide entire herds of Stantler, sensing safe routes through difficult terrain while its strong legs carry it across snow, hills, and other obstacles. The species was deeply respected by Hisuian people, and one special Wyrdeer descended from a Pokemon blessed by Arceus served humans as a Ride Pokemon. Wyrdeer is no longer known from modern wild populations, suggesting that the conditions allowing Stantler to develop this form have largely disappeared.

playthrough: Smeargle is one of the strangest playthrough Pokemon ever designed because its base stats are extremely poor but Sketch allows it to permanently copy almost any move used in front of it. This means a deliberately trained Smeargle can theoretically assemble combinations unavailable to almost any other Pokemon—sleep through Spore, recovery, Baton Pass, hazards, setup, fixed-damage attacks, utility, or even field moves—yet acquiring those moves requires careful preparation and often exposing fragile Smeargle to the Pokemon using them. Its base 20 Attack and Special Attack make ordinary damaging moves weak even when they are powerful on other species, while 55/35/45 bulk and base 75 Speed leave little room for mistakes during direct combat. Smeargle therefore performs best as a custom-built support Pokemon rather than an attacker, and in casual story play the effort required to engineer the ideal Sketch targets can outweigh the benefit compared with simply using naturally stronger Pokemon. For players willing to plan around Sketch, however, no other ordinary species offers comparable freedom to design an entirely personalized four-move support set.
competitive: Smeargle has one of the most unusual competitive histories in Pokemon because almost every one of its base stats is terrible, yet Sketch gives it access to nearly every move in the game. Across generations it has built serious niches around Spore, Baton Pass, Spikes, Stealth Rock, Sticky Web, Shell Smash, Quiver Dance, Ingrain, Belly Drum, Endeavor, Trick Room, and countless other combinations that would be impossible on a normal Pokemon. In GSC it pioneered trap-and-pass or Agility Baton Pass strategies, ADV expanded its Baton Pass and Spikes roles, and later generations repeatedly forced competitive rules to account for strategies involving Baton Pass or Moody; modern Smeargle still appears as a dedicated hazard and disruption lead despite sitting in very low usage tiers. Focus Sash is especially important in later generations because Smeargle's poor bulk often means surviving one hit is all it needs to put something to sleep or establish a key hazard. Its competitive legacy is therefore almost entirely movepool-driven: Smeargle succeeds not by winning stat-for-stat battles, but by doing combinations of strategic tasks that no other Pokemon is legally capable of compressing into one moveset.
nuzlocke: Smeargle is a high-effort, high-risk Nuzlocke Pokemon because its almost unlimited movepool is paired with defenses too weak to tolerate many mistakes. A carefully prepared Smeargle can learn exceptional safety tools such as Spore, recovery, Protect, priority, fixed-damage attacks, Substitute, screens, or other specialized moves through Sketch, potentially creating a set tailored to a particular boss fight. The problem is that setting up those moves safely can itself be dangerous, and Smeargle's low offenses mean it often depends on status, fixed damage, or teammates rather than defeating opponents directly. Its pure Normal typing at least provides a Ghost immunity and only a Fighting weakness, but strong neutral attacks can still be fatal because of its 55/35/45 bulk. Smeargle can reward a highly technical Nuzlocke player with extraordinary customization, but for an ordinary run it is usually much less reliable than a naturally stronger Pokemon that requires no elaborate Sketch preparation.

pokemon.name: Smeargle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Smeargle produces a mysterious paint-like fluid from the tip of its brush-shaped tail, with the basic color determined individually and the intensity of that color capable of changing with the Pokemon's emotional state. It uses the fluid extensively to mark territory and express itself, and more than five thousand distinct Smeargle markings have been documented; especially unusual symbols can become valuable collectors' items among human enthusiasts. Upon reaching adulthood, Smeargle commonly allow companions to place paint-covered footprints on their backs, creating the characteristic mark associated with mature individuals. The species is frequently found in urban environments covered with graffiti, where territorial painting and artistic expression naturally overlap. Its biological paint behavior is mirrored by Sketch, the unique ability to observe another Pokemon's technique and permanently reproduce that move as part of its own repertoire.

name: Leafeon
biologyAndBehavior: Leafeon's fur contains cells that behave more like plant cells than ordinary animal tissue, allowing it to obtain energy through photosynthesis rather than relying entirely on food. While resting in sunlight it also purifies the surrounding air, and it is commonly described as a peaceful Pokemon that prefers avoiding combat. When friends are threatened, however, Leafeon can harden and sharpen its leaf-like tail into a cutting weapon whose edge is said to exceed that of a manufactured sword and can sever a large tree in a single strike. Its biology therefore combines an unusually passive, plantlike lifestyle with formidable defensive weaponry used primarily when protection is necessary.
playthrough: Leafeon combines excellent 130 Defense with 110 Attack and respectable 95 Speed, giving it an unusual mixture of physical durability and offensive pressure. Strong physical Grass STAB such as Leaf Blade lets it handle Water-, Ground-, and Rock-types effectively while taking physical attacks much better than its appearance might suggest. Its primary limitations are pure Grass typing, weak 65 Special Defense, and a relatively shallow coverage movepool, leaving it vulnerable to numerous common types and special coverage attacks. Its usefulness also depends on team composition, since Grass starters and other readily available Grass-types can make spending Eevee on Leafeon redundant.
competitive: Leafeon's 130 Defense, 110 Attack, and 95 Speed allow it to function as either a physically defensive Pokemon or an offensive threat, but its pure Grass typing and limited coverage restrict both roles. It can check certain physical Ground-, Water-, and Grass-type attackers while still threatening opponents with its respectable Attack rather than becoming completely passive. Chlorophyll provides an alternative offensive niche by doubling its Speed in sun, allowing Leafeon to operate as a fast physical sweeper when supported by the appropriate weather. Competition from Grass-types with better secondary typings, coverage, abilities, or utility has generally kept Leafeon from establishing itself consistently in higher competitive tiers.
nuzlocke: Leafeon's 130 Defense gives it excellent safety against known physical attackers, particularly Water-, Ground-, and Rock-types that it can also threaten with strong Grass STAB. Its 95 Speed and 110 Attack are valuable because Leafeon does not have to rely entirely on defensive stalling and can often remove favorable opponents quickly. However, its 65 Special Defense and numerous Grass weaknesses make unexpected special coverage particularly dangerous, especially in blind runs where enemy movesets are unknown. Leafeon consequently performs best when encounters can be planned in advance and its strong physical matchups can be exploited without exposing it to special Fire-, Ice-, Flying-, Bug-, or Poison-type attacks.

name: Glaceon
biologyAndBehavior: Glaceon can deliberately lower its body temperature to approximately -75 degrees Fahrenheit, freezing its fur into needle-like icicles that can be fired at threats or prey. The same temperature control allows it to freeze atmospheric moisture almost instantly, producing ice crystals, diamond-dust flurries, and powdery snow. It can even surround food with ice pellets, while its frozen fur serves as protection when it sleeps. The glittering snowfall it creates is beautiful enough to distract observers before they realize they are being frozen, and humans make practical use of Glaceon's snow-producing ability at ski resorts.
playthrough: Glaceon's 130 Special Attack makes its Ice-type attacks extremely powerful, giving it strong offensive matchups against Dragon-, Flying-, Grass-, and Ground-types that can become especially valuable late in many games. Contrary to its reputation as a conventional glass cannon, 110 Defense and 95 Special Defense give it respectable raw defenses, but 65 HP, 65 Speed, and pure Ice typing make that bulk difficult to exploit consistently. Its low Speed frequently forces it to absorb an attack before retaliating, while weaknesses to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel expose it to several common offensive types. Availability has also historically hurt Glaceon's playthrough value, as some games place the location or method required to evolve Eevee into Glaceon very late in the main story.
competitive: Glaceon functions primarily as a slow special wallbreaker, using its enormous 130 Special Attack to threaten heavy damage with moves such as Ice Beam and Blizzard. Freeze-Dry significantly improves its offensive profile in later generations by allowing an Ice-type attack to hit Water-types super effectively, reducing one of the traditional limitations of relying heavily on Ice STAB. Its respectable defensive stats are undermined by pure Ice typing, low Speed, entry-hazard vulnerability in relevant generations, and limited coverage, making it difficult to position safely against offensive teams. Glaceon can be extremely threatening once given an opportunity to attack, but faster and more versatile special wallbreakers generally provide similar damage with fewer structural weaknesses.
nuzlocke: Glaceon's powerful Ice STAB can provide an important answer to dangerous Dragons and other Ice-weak bosses, and its 110 Defense means it can survive many neutral physical attacks better than its reputation suggests. The problem is that pure Ice typing provides very little defensive utility while creating weaknesses to several common attacking types, and its 65 Speed means Glaceon often has to withstand a hit before acting. This makes matchup knowledge especially important: against a known Ice-weak opponent without dangerous coverage, Glaceon can be an excellent specialist, while unexpected Fighting-, Rock-, Steel-, or Fire-type attacks can make it risky. Late evolution availability in some games further reduces its Nuzlocke value because Eevee may need to remain unevolved for a significant portion of the run.

name: Sylveon
biologyAndBehavior: Sylveon's ribbon-like feelers are highly mobile sensory organs that emit an aura capable of suppressing hostility, sometimes ending fights without direct combat. It commonly wraps these feelers around a trusted Trainer's arm, allowing it to sense the person's emotions while they walk together. The same calming ability has a predatory use: Sylveon can lower a target's aggression and distract it with swirling feelers before suddenly pouncing. Despite its gentle and affectionate behavior toward companions, Sylveon is notably fearless against Dragon Pokemon and has been described charging opponents many times its own size without hesitation.
playthrough: Fairy is an outstanding story-mode typing, and Sylveon provides reliable answers to Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-types while possessing enough Special Attack to remove enemies rather than merely wall them. Its 95 HP and exceptional 130 Special Defense make it forgiving against special attackers, while its 110 Special Attack provides strong offensive pressure despite its low Speed. Pixilate can turn Normal-type attacks into powerful Fairy-type moves in games where the Hidden Ability is available, further increasing its damage potential. Its main vulnerabilities are weak physical Defense and poor Speed, making strong physical Poison- and Steel-type attackers particularly dangerous.
competitive: Depending on the format, Sylveon can function as either a Wish-supporting special wall or a powerful Pixilate Hyper Voice attacker. Historically, its excellent special bulk and Fairy typing have allowed it to check Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-types while supporting teammates with moves such as Wish and, in generations where available, Heal Bell. Offensive sets exploit 110 Special Attack and Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice to deal substantial Fairy-type damage while retaining far more natural bulk than many dedicated wallbreakers. Its low Speed, mediocre physical Defense, and competition from other powerful Fairy-types limit its universal viability, but the combination of offense, special bulk, and support gives Sylveon considerable role flexibility.
nuzlocke: Sylveon combines excellent special bulk, useful resistances, a Dragon immunity, strong offense, and good recovery and support options with relatively little reliance on setup. Its durability makes unexpected special attacks and neutral hits less dangerous, while Fairy typing provides valuable offensive and defensive matchups against several threatening types. Unlike more passive defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon, Sylveon can also deal substantial direct damage, allowing it to end dangerous battles instead of relying primarily on status or stalling. Its main concern is the physical side, where 65 Defense and low Speed can leave it exposed to strong Steel-, Poison-, or neutral physical attacks.
